review_metadata.scope: Complete N3 review: 81 word-only cards (CR050-CR130) + 80 curated N3 reference-only targets (CR131-CR210) + 68 reference-only N1 reclassifications + builder.py fallback policy

word_only_reviews.original_ja: その党は急激にのびた。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The party gained ground rapidly.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 今回の選挙でその党は議席を増やした。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: That party increased its seats in this election.
word_only_reviews.notes: その党は急激にのびた is vague and unnatural (支持率が伸びた or 議席を増やした is how people actually talk about political parties).

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 日本では米が主食です。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The main diet in Japan is rice.
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Rice is the staple food in Japan.
word_only_reviews.notes: Confirmed reading こめ; tightened English ('staple food' for 主食).

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 私達は平和を願う。
word_only_reviews.original_en: We long for peace.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: みんなが平和を願っている。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Everyone wishes for peace.
word_only_reviews.notes: 私達は平和を願う sounds like translated English. みんなが平和を願っている is much more natural.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 昨年は雪が少なかった。
word_only_reviews.original_en: There was little snow last year.
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: There wasn't much snow last year.
word_only_reviews.notes: Good, natural sentence.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 牡丹餅で腰打つ。
word_only_reviews.original_en: His bread is buttered on both sides.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 転んで床に強く頭を打った。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I slipped and hit my head hard on the floor.
word_only_reviews.notes: 牡丹餅で腰打つ is an obscure Edo-period proverb nobody uses today. Replaced with natural everyday usage.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: その王は島を治めた。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The king reigned over the island.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 夏休みにフェリーで小さな島へ行った。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I took a ferry to a small island over summer vacation.
word_only_reviews.notes: Replaced fairy-tale prose ('The king reigned over the island') with everyday modern Japanese.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: あのサッカーボールは本物の革でできている。
word_only_reviews.original_en: That football is made of genuine leather.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: この靴は本物の革でできている。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: These shoes are made of genuine leather.
word_only_reviews.notes: Modern soccer balls aren't made of leather anymore; swapping サッカーボール for 靴 or カバン makes it feel contemporary.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 実質成長と名目成長率の差は物価上昇を意味する。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Price increases explain the difference between the real and nominal growth rates.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 最近、ワクチンの接種率が下がっているらしい。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I hear the vaccination rate has been dropping lately.
word_only_reviews.notes: Replaced macroeconomics textbook definition with natural everyday conversation.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: ２日で３つの州を走破した。
word_only_reviews.original_en: We covered three states in two days.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 車で２日間かけて３つの州を横断した。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: We drove across three states in two days.
word_only_reviews.notes: 走破した is slightly stiff/athletic; 横断した is more natural for a road trip, though original is acceptable.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 母に葉書を送った。
word_only_reviews.original_en: I sent my mother a postcard.
word_only_reviews.notes: Clean and natural.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 箱の形は普通四角です。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The shape of a box is usually square.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: このクッキー、星の形をしていて可愛いね。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: These cookies are shaped like stars—so cute!
word_only_reviews.notes: 箱の形は普通四角です is robotic textbook filler. ～の形をしている is how 形 is naturally used.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 正方形には四つの辺がある。
word_only_reviews.original_en: A square has four sides.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: この辺に美味しいラーメン屋ない？
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Are there any good ramen places around here?
word_only_reviews.notes: While 辺 (side of a polygon) is valid geometry, 99% of daily N3 usage of 辺 (へん) is この辺 / その辺 ('around here / that area').

word_only_reviews.original_ja: この磁場の線が２極で北の磁力と南の磁力の間に走っています。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The lines of this field run between magnetic north and magnetic south at the two poles.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: その秘密を知っているのは極一部の人だけだ。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Only a very small number of people know that secret.
word_only_reviews.notes: MISMATCH: Header specifies 極 (ごく), while the clumsy physics sentence uses きょく (magnetic poles). Replaced with natural modern Japanese for ごく (極一部).

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 彼女はかなりの量の酒を飲んだ。
word_only_reviews.original_en: She has had quite a lot to drink.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: このお店はランチの量がすごく多い。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: The lunch portions at this place are huge.
word_only_reviews.notes: かなりの量の酒 sounds like a police report. Talking about food portions (量が多い / 少ない) is classic everyday Japanese.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 塵も積もれば山となる。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Many a little makes a mickle.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 夜のうちに雪がだいぶ積もったね。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Quite a bit of snow piled up overnight, didn't it?
word_only_reviews.notes: 塵も積もれば山となる is a proverb ('mickle' is archaic English); learners first need 積もる for snow/dust piling up.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 川は山から下って湾に注いでいる。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The river descends from the mountains to the bay below.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: ホテルの窓から東京湾がきれいに見えた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: We had a great view of Tokyo Bay from the hotel window.
word_only_reviews.notes: Replaced geography-textbook prose with natural modern context.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 官僚は旧法規の改正に関して、成り行きを見守っています。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Bureaucrats are testing the waters over revising old regulations.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 旧モデルの方がデザインが好きだったな。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I liked the design of the old model better.
word_only_reviews.notes: 官僚は旧法規の改正に関して... is heavy N1 bureaucracy jargon. 旧モデル (old/previous model) is how people use 旧 in real life.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 橋は開通している。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The bridge is open to traffic.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: あの橋を渡ると駅に着くよ。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Cross that bridge and you'll be at the station.
word_only_reviews.notes: 橋を渡る is much more natural for everyday N3 than 開通している.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 人の口には戸は立てられず。
word_only_reviews.original_en: We cannot control the tongues of others.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 風が強いから、しっかり戸を閉めてね。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: The wind is strong, so make sure to shut the door tightly.
word_only_reviews.notes: Replaced classical negative proverb (立てられず) with everyday spoken Japanese.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: この川の幅が１マイルある。
word_only_reviews.original_en: This river is one mile across.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: この道は幅が狭くて車が通れない。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: This road is too narrow for cars to get through.
word_only_reviews.notes: この川の幅が１マイルある has awkward particle usage (が instead of は) and uses miles. 幅が狭い / 幅が広い is natural Japanese.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 河を小舟で渡った。
word_only_reviews.original_en: We crossed the river in a small boat.
word_only_reviews.notes: Good sentence.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 売れ行きは目標に達しなかった。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Sales fell short of their goal.
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Sales fell short of the target.
word_only_reviews.notes: Natural business/everyday Japanese.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 猫は背を弓なりに曲げた。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The cat arched its back.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: いつの間にか息子に背を抜かれた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Before I knew it, my son had grown taller than me.
word_only_reviews.notes: 背が高い / 背が伸びる / 背を抜かれる is how standalone 背 (せ) is used in modern conversation (physical 'back' is 背中 [せなか]).

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 船は水路を下った。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The ship sailed down the channel.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 波が高くて船がかなり揺れた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: The waves were high and the boat rocked quite a bit.
word_only_reviews.notes: Replaced literary 水路を下った with natural everyday speech.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 艱難汝を玉にす。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Adversity makes a man wise, not rich.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: うどんを一玉だけ買って帰った。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I bought just one portion of udon noodles on my way home.
word_only_reviews.notes: 艱難汝を玉にす (かんなんなんじをたまにす) is classical literary Japanese. うどんを一玉（ひとたま） maintains pure たま reading without rendaku (unlike 百円玉 ひゃくえんだま).

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 波に足をすくわれた。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The waves carried me off my feet.
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: A wave swept my feet out from under me.
word_only_reviews.notes: Natural Japanese; modernized English.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 帯に短し、襷に長し。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Too much spoils, too little is nothing.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 一人で着物の帯を結ぶのは難しい。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Tying a kimono sash by yourself is hard.
word_only_reviews.notes: Replaced classical proverb (短し/長し) with natural modern Japanese.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 何百羽とキジを撃った。
word_only_reviews.original_en: We shot pheasants by the hundred.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 庭にきれいな鳥の羽が落ちていた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: There was a pretty bird feather lying in the yard.
word_only_reviews.notes: MISMATCH: Header specifies 羽 (はね - feather/wing), while the pheasant-hunting sentence uses わ (counter for birds). Replaced with a natural sentence for はね.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: よし！掃討完了！
word_only_reviews.original_en: Alright! They're all mopped up!
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: ホテルの予約が完了しました。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: The hotel reservation is complete.
word_only_reviews.notes: 掃討完了 ('mopping up the enemy complete') is military/video-game slang. 予約が完了しました is everyday modern usage.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 遠方に城が見えた。
word_only_reviews.original_en: We saw a castle in the distance.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 電車の窓から白いお城が見えた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I saw a white castle from the train window.
word_only_reviews.notes: 遠方に (in the distance) is stiff literary prose.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: あの人は仏のような人だ。
word_only_reviews.original_en: He is a saint of a man.
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: That person is a total saint.
word_only_reviews.notes: Natural idiom; updated English.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 彼は永久に日本を離れた。
word_only_reviews.original_en: He left Japan for good.
word_only_reviews.notes: Confirmed.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 坂を下りるときに彼女のおんぼろ自転車はキーキー音を立てた。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Her old bike squeaked as she rode down the hill.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 駅の近くは急な坂が多くて自転車だと大変だ。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: There are a lot of steep hills near the station, so it's tough by bike.
word_only_reviews.notes: 彼女のおんぼろ自転車... reads like translated English fiction. Replaced with natural everyday speech.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 底を持ってくれ。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Grab the bottom.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 箱の底が抜けそうだから、下を持って。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: The bottom of the box looks like it's going to give out, so hold it from underneath.
word_only_reviews.notes: Original is okay when moving boxes, though adding context makes it much clearer.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: これが彼の泊っているお寺です。
word_only_reviews.original_en: This is the temple where he stays.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 京都で有名なお寺をいくつか回った。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I visited several famous temples in Kyoto.
word_only_reviews.notes: 泊っている has non-standard okurigana (usually 泊まっている) and staying at a temple is rare compared to visiting one.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 息を止めて鼻をつまみなさい。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Hold your breath and pinch your nostrils.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 階段を駆け上がったら息が切れた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I ran up the stairs and got out of breath.
word_only_reviews.notes: 息が切れる / 息を吸う is much more natural than 'Hold your breath and pinch your nostrils'.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 巨大な肉の塊が当たった。
word_only_reviews.original_en: I was hit by a huge chunk of meat.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 駅前に巨大なショッピングモールができた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: They built a huge shopping mall in front of the station.
word_only_reviews.notes: 'I was hit by a huge chunk of meat' is bizarre! Replaced with normal everyday conversation.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 彼の依頼は命令に等しかった。
word_only_reviews.original_en: His request was equivalent to an order.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 新しい仕事の依頼がメールで届いた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: A request for a new job came in by email.
word_only_reviews.notes: Original is acceptable, though 仕事の依頼が届いた is much more common in daily life.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: あれはとても複雑な機械だ。
word_only_reviews.original_en: That is a very complex machine.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 手続きが複雑でよくわからない。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: The procedure is so complicated I don't really get it.
word_only_reviews.notes: Original is okay; 手続きが複雑 or 複雑な気持ち is much more colloquial.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 嫁と姑の仲は大嵐。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law are a tempest and hailstorm.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: あの二人は昔からすごく仲がいいよね。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Those two have gotten along great for ages, haven't they?
word_only_reviews.notes: Replaced dramatic soap-opera line with natural everyday Japanese (仲がいい).

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 彼は店の入り口に閉店の札をかけた。
word_only_reviews.original_en: He put a Closed sign on the front door of the store.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 財布に千円札が一枚しか入っていない。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I only have a single 1,000-yen bill in my wallet.
word_only_reviews.notes: MISMATCH: Header specifies 札 (さつ - banknote), while the sentence uses ふだ (sign/placard). Provided a natural sentence for さつ. (If the card actually wants ふだ, confirm the original sentence with reading ふだ).

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 犬はよく骨を地面に埋める。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Dogs often bury bones.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 魚の骨が喉に刺さってしまった。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I got a fish bone stuck in my throat.
word_only_reviews.notes: 魚の骨が喉に刺さる is super common and natural in Japan (and avoids rendaku in 小骨 こぼね).

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 子供は積み木で遊ぶ。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Children play with blocks.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 週末は友達と遊んでばかりいた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I did nothing but hang out with friends over the weekend.
word_only_reviews.notes: Confirmed reading あそぶ; provided a more colloquial alternative.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 君には前途がある。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Life lies in front of you.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: この仕事、君に任せてもいいかな？
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Can I leave this job to you?
word_only_reviews.notes: 前途がある is old-fashioned. Replaced with natural modern conversational usage.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 島は濃い霧に包まれていた。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The island was enveloped in a thick fog.
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: The island was wrapped in thick fog.
word_only_reviews.notes: Good sentence.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 緑は草を連想させる。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Green is associated with grass.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 雨が続いて、庭の草があっという間に伸びた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: With all the rain, the grass in the yard grew in no time.
word_only_reviews.notes: 庭の草が伸びた / 草むしりをする is how 草 is used in real life.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 生地を預ければドレスを仕立ててくれますか。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Will you make me up a dress if I give you the material?
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: チェックインの前に、フロントで荷物を預けた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I left my luggage at the front desk before checking in.
word_only_reviews.notes: Nobody commissions a tailor with bolt fabric anymore; 荷物を預ける is essential everyday travel Japanese.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 泉はおよそ１７０フィートの高さまで温水を吹き出す。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The fountain sends hot water to a height of 170 feet.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 森の奥にきれいな泉が湧いている。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: There's a clear spring bubbling up deep in the forest.
word_only_reviews.notes: Original is a clumsy translation of a geyser (間欠泉) using feet.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 夏にお祭りがある。
word_only_reviews.original_en: There is a festival in the summer.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 今週末、駅前でお祭りがあるらしいよ。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: I hear there's a festival in front of the station this weekend.
word_only_reviews.notes: Confirmed reading; added optional conversational polish.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 男は袋を肩に担いだ。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The man threw a bag across his shoulder.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 袋にお入れしますか？
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Would you like this in a bag?
word_only_reviews.notes: 袋にお入れしますか is heard every single day at Japanese convenience stores.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 私の娘は分娩中だ。
word_only_reviews.original_en: My daughter is in labor.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: うちの娘は今年から高校生になります。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: Our daughter is starting high school this year.
word_only_reviews.notes: 分娩中 (in obstetric labor) is medical terminology. うちの娘 is how parents naturally refer to their daughter.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 塩は目方で売られる。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Salt is sold by weight.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 味が薄いから、もう少し塩を足そう。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: It's a bit bland, so let's add a little more salt.
word_only_reviews.notes: 目方 (めかた — weight) is archaic Showa/Meiji vocabulary.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 彼は腕が上がった。
word_only_reviews.original_en: He has improved in skill.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 彼、最近すごく料理の腕が上がったよね。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: His cooking skills have really leveled up lately, haven't they?
word_only_reviews.notes: 腕が上がる is a great idiom; adding 料理の makes it immediately clear.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 朝は気温が零下になった。
word_only_reviews.original_en: The temperature dropped below zero in the morning.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 今朝は冷え込んで、気温が零下になった。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: It got freezing this morning and the temperature dropped below zero.
word_only_reviews.notes: CRITICAL READING ERROR IN DRAFT: 零下 is read れいか, NEVER れいした!

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 彼は青筋を立てて怒った。
word_only_reviews.original_en: He was so angry that his veins stood out.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 約束の時間に遅れたら、彼女にめちゃくちゃ怒られた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: She got super mad at me when I showed up late.
word_only_reviews.notes: Original is okay (idiomatic), or use a more casual everyday sentence.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 彼の考えはとても幼い。
word_only_reviews.original_en: His way of thinking is very childish.
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: His way of thinking is really immature.
word_only_reviews.notes: Confirmed reading おさない; 'immature' fits 考えが幼い better.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 彼の甘い口車にのるな。
word_only_reviews.original_en: Don't fall for his sugar-coated words.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 疲れた時はやっぱり甘いものが食べたくなる。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: When I'm tired, I always crave something sweet.
word_only_reviews.notes: 口車に乗る is good idiomatic Japanese, though 甘いものが食べたくなる is more common in daily conversation.

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 私は大臣自身と話した。
word_only_reviews.original_en: I spoke to the minister himself.
word_only_reviews.corrected_ja: 新しい大臣が記者会見を開いた。
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: The new minister held a press conference.
word_only_reviews.notes: 大臣自身と話した sounds like literal translationese ('the minister himself').

word_only_reviews.original_ja: 彼は医者の卵だ。
word_only_reviews.original_en: He's a future doctor.
word_only_reviews.corrected_en: He's a doctor in training.
